chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar (may God be pleased with him) narrated that his father quoted Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Imran al-Ash'ari, on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of some of our companions, on the authority of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ten parts of a sheep should not be eaten: the feces; the blood; the spleen; the bone marrow; the glands; the penis; the testicles; the womb; the vagina; the veins, or he said: the blood vessels.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten parts of a sheep that should not be eaten according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) detailing ten specific anatomical parts of the sheep deemed impure or undesirable for consumption, reflecting the Shia emphasis on both ritual purity (taharah) and physical health in dietary laws. The slight variation in the final term—either 'blood vessels' (al-awrad) or 'trachea/esophagus' (al-udaj)—highens the scholarly attention to precise anatomical identification in fiqh. This list complements the general prohibition of blood by specifying particular organs and tissues that carry distinct impurities or health implications.
